questions.stem: A reaction has reactants at 400 kJ and products at 150 kJ. What is the enthalpy change (ΔH) for this reaction?
questions.explanation: ΔH is calculated as energy of products minus energy of reactants: ΔH = 150 - 400 = -250 kJ. The negative value indicates this is an exothermic reaction, with products at a lower energy level than reactants.

questions.stem: On an energy level diagram, the y-axis represents energy and the x-axis represents the progress of reaction. What does the vertical distance between the reactant and product lines represent?

options.text: The activation energy of the reaction
The enthalpy change (ΔH) of the reaction
The temperature change during the reaction

questions.explanation: The vertical distance between the reactant and product energy levels on an energy level diagram represents the enthalpy change (ΔH) of the reaction. It shows the overall energy difference between reactants and products.
